new_statements.quote: [p. 1:] ごく少数の単語を除き、浅間方言の各語形は少なくとも一つの重音節（長母音か二重母音を含むか、撥音か促音で終る音節）がなければならない。重音節の位置と音調型を基準にすると浅間方言の多くの単純名詞は共時的に次の三つの語類に分類できる｡ [p. 2:] 浅間方言のA語類の単語は語頭から高く、第二拍を含む音節は重音節である。B語類は語末音節が重音節で、四拍以下の単語の場合は語末拍が、五拍の単語の場合は語末音節が高い。C語類は前語末拍を含む音節が重音節で、四拍以下の単語の場合は語末拍が、五拍の単語の場合は語末音節が高い｡
new_statements.translation: [p. 1:] Apart from a very small number of words, every word form of the Asama dialect must contain at least one heavy syllable (a syllable containing a long vowel or diphthong, or ending in a moraic nasal or geminate). On the basis of the position of the heavy syllable and the tone pattern, most simple nouns of the Asama dialect can be classified synchronically into the following three word classes. [p. 2:] Words of class A in the Asama dialect are high from the beginning of the word, and the syllable containing the second mora is heavy. In class B the word-final syllable is heavy, and the final mora (for words of four or fewer moras) or the final syllable (for five-mora words) is high. In class C the syllable containing the penultimate mora is heavy, and the final mora (four or fewer moras) or the final syllable (five-mora words) is high.

Adds weight-conditioned three-class noun tone; compatible with Hayata's two-register analysis (Lawrence's A = high register; B and C = low register split by heavy-syllable position).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-level tone: nouns fall into three classes defined jointly by where the obligatory heavy syllable sits and by the pitch pattern — A = high-register (high from the first syllable; Lawrence argues in §2 that whether it later falls is predictable, so high-register is a single pattern, 一型); B and C = low-register with the rise on the final mora (≤4 moras) or final syllable (5 moras). Foot structure (moraic trochee / iambic feet) is used to derive compound and diminutive tone. No mention of stress.
new_statements.exceptions: 'A very small number of words' lack a heavy syllable; minimal pairs like ha[n]dai 阪大 vs ha[n]dai 飯台 among high-register nouns, which Lawrence argues are predictable from structure; diminutives in -gama of class-A (C)Vi monosyllables and (C)VCV: disyllables become low-register.

tone_statements.quote: Isen is a pitch accent language where H and L are distinguished. Nouns have a three-way distinction; that is, each noun lexically has one of the three tonal patterns (Hirayama et al. 1966). (5) shows the ternary accentual distinction among bimoraic nouns. (5) a. A vs. B: /kóó/ HH ‘river’, /kòó/ LH ‘skin’ b. A vs. C: /hásí/ HH ‘bridge’, /hásì/ HL ‘chopsticks’ c. B vs. C: /kàmɨ́/ LH ‘turtle’, /kámɨ̀/ HL ‘pot’ … Verbs have a two-way accentual distinction: one class of verbs has a rising pitch contour and the other lacks this rise.

tone_statements.quote: その結果、調査した 19 方言の名詞アクセントは「モーラを数えの単位とする、昇り核を持つ３型、もしくは４型アクセント」の体系を持つことが明らかになった。また、徳之島諸方言の名詞アクセントを、大きくイ群、ロ群、ハ群に分類し、イ群は X 型(“０”)、Y 型(“-1”)、Z 型(“-2”)の 3 型アクセント体系を持ち、ロ群は X 型(“０”)、Y 型(“-1”)、W 型(+3)、Z 型(“-2”)、ハ群の浅間方言は X 型(“０”)、V 型(“+4”)、Y 型(“-1”)を持つとした。 [§1.1, p. 1:] これまで、徳之島諸方言のアクセントは多型アクセント体系、もしくは語声調の方言であると記述されてきた。
tone_statements.translation: As a result, it became clear that the noun accent of the 19 dialects surveyed has a system of 'three-pattern or four-pattern accent with a rising kernel, counted in morae'. The noun accent of the Tokunoshima dialects was classified broadly into groups I, RO and HA: group I has a three-pattern system of type X ('0'), type Y ('-1') and type Z ('-2'); group RO has X ('0'), Y ('-1'), W ('+3') and Z ('-2'); and the Asama dialect (group HA) has X ('0'), V ('+4') and Y ('-1'). [§1.1:] Until now the accent of the Tokunoshima dialects has been described as a multi-pattern (N-kei) accent system or as word-tone dialects.

tone_statements.quote: 資料は語形の長さや音調により分類し、高起式（1a-g）の後に低起式（1h-k）の語形を、アルファベット順に配列した … 複合語の左端にある最大の韻律単位（拍か韻脚）を韻律外にする。新しく左端にあらわれた最大の韻律単位（拍か韻脚）をとばして、高声調をその次の韻脚の初頭音節に付与する。別の高声調を後部成素内の前語末拍を含む重音節に付与する。単語内に高声調が複数ある場合、その間の拍はすべて高く発音される｡ … 本稿では - ムン名詞の音調を分析して、その音調は単語のモーラ・音節・韻脚構造と前部成素の式（高起・低起）から予測可能であることを論じた。
tone_statements.translation: Data are sorted by length and tone, high-beginning register (1a-g) before low-beginning register (1h-k), alphabetically … The largest prosodic unit (mora or foot) at the compound's left edge is made extraprosodic. Skipping the largest unit now at the left edge, a high tone goes on the first syllable of the next foot. Another high tone goes on the heavy syllable in the second member containing the penultimate mora. With several high tones in a word, all moras between them are high. … I analysed the tone of -mun nouns and argued it is predictable from mora, syllable and foot structure and the first member's register (high-/low-beginning).
tone_statements.locator: p.173 §2; p.183 §3, indented tone-assignment procedure quoted from Lawrence 2016: 2-3; p.184 §5 結語
tone_statements.summary: Word-tone system: every word is lexically high- or low-beginning in register; pitch rises and falls follow from mora, syllable-weight and foot structure; compounds keep the first member's register.

tone_statements.translation: Words that are segmentally identical but contrast in accent are listed as 'Cf.'. … (5) Pitch symbols (○ = any mora): [○ = a rise immediately before ○ (same as my earlier ｢); ○] = a fall immediately after ○ (same as my earlier ｣ or ⌉); %○ = a half-rise immediately before ○ (appears in places like 'handle of the axe'). … The pitch symbol attached at word end is omitted this time (for the interpretation of the accent system, see Uwano 2016).

tone_statements.summary: Lexical pitch accent: words contrast by where pitch rises and falls (plus a half-rise), located by mora; thousands of accent-marked nouns from one speaker; type inventory deferred to Uwano 2016.

Tokyo: 法政大学沖縄文化研究所.
tone_statements.quote: 浅間方言の単純動詞のアクセントは高平調と上昇調という下降のない型のみによる２種類の対立であるのに対して、複合動詞には下降を伴う型が現われ、３音節語には５つ、４音節語では６つの対立がある。そのアクセントは、前部要素単独形の高平調/上昇調に応じて、それぞれ高く始まる/低く始まるが決まる式保存の関係がある。 … (3)(4)は、高平調(上欄)と上昇調(下欄)の２つに分かれる。このうちの上昇調は、４モーラ語(音節数では２音節語○○と３音節語oo○)までは最後の１モーラだけが高い型(-[N)であるのに対して、５モーラ語(３音節語○o○、４音節語ooo○)では最後の２モーラが高い-[(C)juNの形を取る … (19)(a)高く始まるもの：Aグループ (b)低く始まり、(可能な限り最後の)２モーラが高くなるもの：Bグループ (c)低く始まり、１モーラだけ高くなるもの：Cグループ … (３４)は、関西諸方言の名詞のアクセント体系に比較的よく似たものとなっている。
tone_statements.translation: Simple-verb accent in Asama is a two-way opposition of fall-less patterns only, high-level vs rising, whereas compound verbs show patterns with a fall: five oppositions in 3-syllable, six in 4-syllable words. Register is preserved: the compound begins high/low as its first element alone is high-level/rising. … (3)(4) split into high-level (upper row) and rising (lower row); the rising type has only the last mora high (-[N) up to 4 morae …, the last two high, -[(C)juN, at 5 morae … (19)(a) begins high: group A; (b) begins low, (last possible) two morae high: B; (c) begins low, one mora high: C … (34) is fairly like Kansai noun accent systems.
tone_statements.summary: Kansai-like register word accent: verbs begin high (high-level) or low (rising, last 1-2 morae high); compound verbs add patterns with a pitch fall and keep the register of their first member.

tone_statements.quote: ［要旨］松原方言の用言(動詞・形容詞)の基本形(終止形)について、アクセント資料を提示し、そのアクセント体系を考える。 … しかしなお、動詞にも体言にも、ａ－ｃ類の３型には納まらない型が１つずつ存在する。 … (20）音調型派生規則(改訂版） a類：第１音節が重音節の時はそこから上げよ。第１音節が軽音節の時は第２音節から上げよ。 … b類：第１音節が重音節の時は第２音節から上げよ。第１音節が軽音節の時は第３音節から上げよ。該当する音節がない場合は、最終音節を上昇調にせよ。 … c類：第１音節が重音節の時は第２音節から上げよ。第１音節が軽音節の時は第３音節から上げよ。該当する音節がない場合は、最終音節を上げよ。上げた後は、語末に可能な限り２モーラを残して下げよ。 …
tone_statements.translation: [Abstract] For Matsubara verb and adjective basic (conclusive) forms I present accent data and consider the accent system. … Yet verbs and nouns each still have one pattern not fitting the three patterns a-c. … (20) Pitch-pattern derivation rules (revised). Class a: 1st syllable heavy: raise from it; light: raise from the 2nd syllable. … Class b: 1st syllable heavy: raise from the 2nd; light: from the 3rd; if no such syllable, make the last syllable rising. … Class c: 1st syllable heavy: raise from the 2nd; light: from the 3rd; if no such syllable, raise the last syllable. Once raised, lower, leaving two morae at word end if possible. …
tone_statements.locator: Abstract [要旨] + keywords, article p.1; rule set (20), sec. 4.6, article p.11; see also (1)-(2) p.1-2
tone_statements.summary: Three-pattern word accent: each word is lexically class a, b or c, realised by a pitch shape (a early rise, b later rise, c rise+fall) set by syllable weight; one residual type; stress unmentioned.

readall_conflicts: No source mentions word stress, so there is no conflict about stress. The sources differ in how they analyse the pitch system: Uwano 1977 (as reported by Hayata 1995, pp. 136–137) treats Asama as an accent dialect in the narrow sense with two registers (high-beginning vs low-beginning) plus a distinctive locus of pitch change; Hayata 1995 (pp. 137–138, 143) rejects this and calls it a two-pattern word-tone system where the pitch shape follows from word tone plus syllable structure; Lawrence 2016 (pp. 1–2) sorts nouns into three classes A/B/C by heavy-syllable position and pitch, treating the high register as a single pattern; Lévêque & Pellard 2019/2023 and the Lévêque 2021 thesis abstract call it a word-tone system with four verbal melodies (H, LH, HL, LHL) conditioned by syllable weight. All agree it is a word-level pitch/tone system interacting with syllable weight, and none uses the category 'stress'.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both the deciding passage (Uwano 2015 sec. 3 p.179) and the supporting register-preservation passage (Uwano 2014 sec. 4 p.143; heavy-syllable definition p.142) are verbatim in the held NINJAL PDFs/text layers at the stated locators. (2) The classification 'tonal' (qv tonal-OR-pitch accent, no stress domain) rests on first-hand accent reports by Uwano, the primary fieldworker on this dialect since 1977; every other source opened — Hayata 1995 ('単語声調方言'), Lawrence 2016 (three lexical tone classes A/B/C, 高起/低起), Lévêque & Pellard 2023 ('word-tone system where melodies are mapped onto whole word forms.. strong interdependence between tone pattern and syllable weight'), and Kato 2022 for the neighbouring Isen dialect ('pitch accent language where H and L are distinguished') — confirms a lexical word-tone/pitch accent system with an obligatory heavy syllable and no stress. sources.quote: Every Asama word form must contain at least one heavy syllable; simple nouns fall into three lexical tone classes A (high from word onset, 2nd-mora syllable heavy), B and C (low-beginning, final mora/syllable high, distinguished by position of the heavy syllable); discusses whether the high-register (高起) class has one or two contrastive patterns. sources.quote: [p. 1:] ごく少数の単語を除き、浅間方言の各語形は少なくとも一つの重音節（長母音か二重母音を含むか、撥音か促音で終る音節）がなければならない。重音節の位置と音調型を基準にすると浅間方言の多くの単純名詞は共時的に次の三つの語類に分類できる｡ [p. 2:] 浅間方言のA語類の単語は語頭から高く、第二拍を含む音節は重音節である。B語類は語末音節が重音節で、四拍以下の単語の場合は語末拍が、五拍の単語の場合は語末音節が高い。C語類は前語末拍を含む音節が重音節で、四拍以下の単語の場合は語末拍が、五拍の単語の場合は語末音節が高い｡

sources.quote: [p. 136–137, on Uwano 1977's analysis:] 氏のこの分析によれば、この方言は音節単位ではあるが、高く始る単語声調'a'（上野氏の高起「式」）と低く始る単語声調'b'（同じく低起式）およびピッチの変り目(高起式の場合は下がり目、低起式の場合は上がり目)の位置が問題になる狭義のアクセント方言で […] 筆者がかつてこれを見て多少分析を試みてみたところ、どう見ても名詞は２型単語声調としか思えない [p. 138:] 筆者としては、（４）の体系は、まず名詞に限れば（動詞については活用表が完備していないと何とも言えない)、（５）のように非常にあっさりした２型単語声調体系に過ぎないということである。 [p. 143:] それでも松原はもとより、浅間の名詞アクセントの体系も単語声調であると筆者は思っている。

sources.quote: 資料は語形の長さや音調により分類し、高起式（1a-g）の後に低起式（1h-k）の語形を、アルファベット順に配列した … 複合語の左端にある最大の韻律単位（拍か韻脚）を韻律外にする。新しく左端にあらわれた最大の韻律単位（拍か韻脚）をとばして、高声調をその次の韻脚の初頭音節に付与する。別の高声調を後部成素内の前語末拍を含む重音節に付与する。単語内に高声調が複数ある場合、その間の拍はすべて高く発音される｡ … 本稿では - ムン名詞の音調を分析して、その音調は単語のモーラ・音節・韻脚構造と前部成素の式（高起・低起）から予測可能であることを論じた。

tone.translation: Data are sorted by length and tone, high-beginning register (1a-g) before low-beginning register (1h-k), alphabetically … The largest prosodic unit (mora or foot) at the compound's left edge is made extraprosodic. Skipping the largest unit now at the left edge, a high tone goes on the first syllable of the next foot. Another high tone goes on the heavy syllable in the second member containing the penultimate mora. With several high tones in a word, all moras between them are high. … I analysed the tone of -mun nouns and argued it is predictable from mora, syllable and foot structure and the first member's register (high-/low-beginning).

sources.quote: 浅間方言の単純動詞のアクセントは高平調と上昇調という下降のない型のみによる２種類の対立であるのに対して、複合動詞には下降を伴う型が現われ、３音節語には５つ、４音節語では６つの対立がある。そのアクセントは、前部要素単独形の高平調/上昇調に応じて、それぞれ高く始まる/低く始まるが決まる式保存の関係がある。 … (3)(4)は、高平調(上欄)と上昇調(下欄)の２つに分かれる。このうちの上昇調は、４モーラ語(音節数では２音節語○○と３音節語oo○)までは最後の１モーラだけが高い型(-[N)であるのに対して、５モーラ語(３音節語○o○、４音節語ooo○)では最後の２モーラが高い-[(C)juNの形を取る … (19)(a)高く始まるもの：Aグループ (b)低く始まり、(可能な限り最後の)２モーラが高くなるもの：Bグループ (c)低く始まり、１モーラだけ高くなるもの：Cグループ … (３４)は、関西諸方言の名詞のアクセント体系に比較的よく似たものとなっている。
sources.note: Kansai-like register word accent: verbs begin high (high-level) or low (rising, last 1-2 morae high); compound verbs add patterns with a pitch fall and keep the register of their first member.

tone.translation: Simple-verb accent in Asama is a two-way opposition of fall-less patterns only, high-level vs rising, whereas compound verbs show patterns with a fall: five oppositions in 3-syllable, six in 4-syllable words. Register is preserved: the compound begins high/low as its first element alone is high-level/rising. … (3)(4) split into high-level (upper row) and rising (lower row); the rising type has only the last mora high (-[N) up to 4 morae …, the last two high, -[(C)juN, at 5 morae … (19)(a) begins high: group A; (b) begins low, (last possible) two morae high: B; (c) begins low, one mora high: C … (34) is fairly like Kansai noun accent systems.

tone.translation: [Abstract] For Matsubara verb and adjective basic (conclusive) forms I present accent data and consider the accent system. … Yet verbs and nouns each still have one pattern not fitting the three patterns a-c. … (20) Pitch-pattern derivation rules (revised). Class a: 1st syllable heavy: raise from it; light: raise from the 2nd syllable. … Class b: 1st syllable heavy: raise from the 2nd; light: from the 3rd; if no such syllable, make the last syllable rising. … Class c: 1st syllable heavy: raise from the 2nd; light: from the 3rd; if no such syllable, raise the last syllable. Once raised, lower, leaving two morae at word end if possible. …
